clue.text: Deep saying, revolutionary, about which there's praise

indicators.note: the praise word sits about, that is around, the turned saying

parts.note: to bless is to praise or glorify

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the word for the saying is read backwards

parts.note: a motto is a short saying or maxim

explanation.surface: A profound remark of radical politics draws applause from its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns MOTTO into OTTOM, and 'about' wraps BLESS around it: B-OTTOM-LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no floor or limit to its depth is unfathomably deep, as in a seemingly endless pit.

clue.text: Object about cutting good climbing plant

parts.note: a butt is the object or target of ridicule, as in the butt of a joke

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the piece is read upwards, that is backwards
the letter for about cuts into the word for good, sitting inside it

parts.note: pure means good, virtuous
C, for circa, is the abbreviation meaning about

explanation.surface: Someone protests about pruning a fine climber in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts C inside PURE to make PUCRE, and 'climbing' turns that upwards to ERCUP after BUTT. The plant is not a climber: 'climbing' is only the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a common yellow-flowered meadow plant of the genus Ranunculus.

clue.text: Next article, new

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An editor lines up the following piece, a fresh one.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb of sequence, it means afterwards or next in order, as in 'first this, then that'.

clue.text: Variety of duties accepted by soldiers becoming stranger

indicators.note: the soldiers take in the rearranged letters, holding them inside

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: a variety of the letters of the word duties means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newcomer to the barracks is given a range of chores by the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges DUTIES into UTSIDE, and 'accepted by' places it inside OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is someone not belonging to a group, a stranger to it.

clue.text: Leader in contest going after record, I sense

indicators.note: the first letter of contest is placed after the record and the I

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of a ship's voyage

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, here of contest

explanation.surface: The front-runner of a competition is placed behind on the scoreboard, as someone sees it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going after' puts C, the first letter of 'contest', after LOG and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is sound reasoning, as in 'there's no sense in that'.

clue.text: Tongs finally grip, holding a vegetable

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of tongs
the word for grip holds the a inside it

parts.note: to pinch is to grip tightly between finger and thumb

explanation.surface: In the kitchen, a pair of tongs at last grasps some greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives S from 'Tongs'; 'holding' puts A inside PINCH, giving PINACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable.

clue.text: Inspector wrong about lawyer being superior

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector

indicators.note: the word for wrong goes about, around, the lawyer

parts.note: sinful means wrong, wicked
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A police officer's mistake involves a prosecutor who is senior to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps SINFUL around DA, giving SDAINFUL after DI. Here 'superior' is an adjective meaning haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior attitude is a scornful, condescending one, looking down on others.

clue.text: Extended species studied

parts.note: sp. is the abbreviation for species in biology
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A naturalist spends a long time examining a particular species.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread out means stretched or extended over a wider area.

clue.text: Eager commitment maintained by demon worker?

parts.note: an imp is a small demon

indicators.note: the commitment is held, maintained, inside the worker

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
a tie is a commitment or obligation

explanation.surface: A keen employee is devoted to a devilishly hard-working colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintained by' puts TIE inside ANT, giving ATIENT after IMP. The question mark warns that 'demon worker' splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless to get started is being keen or eager.

clue.text: Courage to take part in gruelling ritual

indicators.note: take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: It takes bravery to join an exhausting ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is determination and pluck, a form of bravery.

clue.text: Engine conks out — end of the line

parts.note: conks out means stops working, dies

indicators.note: the end of the word the is its final letter

explanation.surface: A motor breaks down at the final stop on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the last letter of 'the', E; 'line' gives L by abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is an engine that ignites its fuel by compression, or a vehicle driven by one.

clue.text: Fish speed round stern

indicators.note: round means turned round, so the speed word is read backwards

parts.note: clip means speed, as in 'at a fair clip'
hard means stern, severe

explanation.surface: A trawler races about the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns CLIP into PILC, then HARD follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilchard is a small oily fish of the herring family, a mature sardine.

clue.text: Destroyed silence, breaking into protest song

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

indicators.note: the call for silence breaks into the song, sitting inside it

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A hush is shattered when chanting starts at a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into' puts SH inside LIED, giving LISHED after DEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something knocked down or wrecked has been destroyed.

clue.text: Elected, expected to embrace Conservative cause

parts.note: a party voted into office is in

indicators.note: the word for expected embraces the letter for Conservative

parts.note: due means expected, as in 'the train is due'

explanation.surface: An elected Tory is expected to take up a political cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embrace' puts C inside DUE, giving DUCE after IN. 'cause' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To induce something is to bring it about or make it happen.

clue.text: Hope to be in the field before start of marathon in part of London

indicators.note: the field piece comes before the first letter of marathon
the word for hope is placed in the field word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field
a wish is a hope

indicators.note: the start of marathon is its first letter

explanation.surface: A runner hopes to be in the leading pack early in the London Marathon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' puts WISH inside LEA, giving LEWISHA, and 'before' puts that ahead of M, the start of 'marathon'. LEWISHAM is a borough of south-east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewisham is a borough in south-east London.

clue.text: Extraordinary fool one upset with variable schedule

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the three pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: rare means extraordinary, uncommon
a nit is a fool, a nitwit
I is the Roman numeral one
Y is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: An eccentric idiot overturns a changeable timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RARE + NIT + I into ITINERAR; the algebra variable Y finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route or timetable for a journey.

clue.text: Just snub idea put in a bad way

indicators.note: putting the letters in a bad way scrambles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Merely rejecting a notion can be done badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in a bad way' rearranges SNUB IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fair and impartial is being just.

clue.text: Fellow with impudent talk long disrespectful

parts.note: lip is cheeky backchat
to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A cheeky chap keeps mouthing off at length.
explanation.definitionFit: Flippant means lacking proper seriousness or respect.

clue.text: Clue, not hard: naughty to trespass

indicators.note: not says the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: a hint is a clue
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
rude means naughty, smutty

explanation.surface: A setter admits an easy, cheeky clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from HINT, leaving INT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter where one is not welcome, to trespass.

clue.text: Get rid of rotten old pies, missing nothing

indicators.note: rotten pies are spoiled, so the letters are mixed up
missing says the letter for nothing is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Throw out the decaying stale pastries, every last one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops O from OLD, leaving LD, and 'rotten' rearranges LD + PIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel is to drive away or banish.

clue.text: Staff with income about to take off

indicators.note: the income word goes about, around, the staff

parts.note: pay is income from work
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees with wages are about to leave on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps PAY around ROD. 'take off' is a noun here, an imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation, as in a take-off of a famous person.

clue.text: See group of three outside hotel with a philanderer

parts.note: lo means look, see

indicators.note: the trio sits outside the letters for hotel and a

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Look: three people staying in a hotel with a womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts TRIO around H + A, giving THARIO after LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, named after a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Backer left after endless vexation

indicators.note: the letter for left comes after the shortened word
endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: anger is vexation

explanation.surface: A sponsor departs after unrelenting irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts R from ANGER.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatrical production.

clue.text: Porcelain presents sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: serves means presents, as of a meal

explanation.surface: Gifts of china are returned to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' is a verb here, not gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevres is fine porcelain made at the French town of that name.

clue.text: Spring skilfully

explanation.surface: A spring is used ably.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a spring of water from the ground; doing something well means doing it skilfully.

clue.text: Called conduct good

parts.note: to run a business is to conduct it

explanation.surface: A summons to behave properly.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past participle of ring, so it means telephoned, as in 'I've rung her'.

clue.text: Leave last piece of work needed by editor in load

indicators.note: the two pieces go in the word for load

parts.note: to saddle someone is to load or burden them

indicators.note: the last piece of work is its final letter

explanation.surface: A journalist must hand in the final article when the editor piles on work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places K (the last letter of 'work') and ED inside SADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run away hurriedly, to make off.

clue.text: Man with money brought about new version of old musical

parts.note: he stands for a man

indicators.note: the money word is brought about, around, the rearranged letters

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money

indicators.note: a new version of the word old rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A rich man funds a revival of a vintage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new version of' turns OLD into LOD, and 'brought about' splits LOLLY around it: L-LOD-OLLY. 'Lolly' is British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A Broadway show of 1964 by Jerry Herman, it is a classic stage production with songs.
